glorice_phsc_ex.notes: Licence CC BY 4.0 on the figshare data record; the accompanying Scientific Data article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, which applies to the paper and not to the data. Contains exten_phsc_{year}.nc for 1961-2021, netCDF4, 5 arcmin, 2160x4320, EPSG:4326, variable 'area' in hectares per cell, NaN where no rice. gaia_1985_2022.product: GAIA annual global artificial impervious area, 30 m, year-of-first-imperviousness encoding
gaia_1985_2022.version: figshare version 1 of the record (10.6084/m9.figshare.27245775.v1); the archive is named GAIA_1985_2022.zip and its readme is headed Version 2022, but the data stops at 2021, so the archive name overstates the coverage by one year
gaia_1985_2022.citation: Gong, P., Li, X., Wang, J., Bai, Y., Chen, B., Hu, T., Liu, X., Xu, B., Yang, J., Zhang, W., & Zhou, Y. (2020). Annual maps of global artificial impervious area (GAIA) between 1985 and 2018. Remote Sensing of Environment, 236, 111510. doi:10.1016/j.rse.2019.111510
gaia_1985_2022.licence: CC BY 4.0, as stated on the figshare record
gaia_1985_2022.notes: Pixel values encode the year a pixel first became impervious, counting downward from the newest year: year equals 2023 minus value, 0 is non-urban, 2 is 2021 and 38 is 1985 and before. Value 1 is never used in the nine tiles retrieved. Nodata is -128 and is not documented in the product readme, which lists only 0 and 2 through 38. Tiles carry a 30 m merge buffer and therefore overlap, so pixels must be clipped to each tile's nominal five-degree extent before counting. The archive sha256 is null because the 2.3 GB zip was deleted after the nine study-box tiles were extracted and no checksum was computed first; it MUST be recorded on re-fetch. The archive is not internally addressable over its distribution route, so re-obtaining any single tile requires the full 2.3 GB fetch. The nine committed tile checksums below are of the extracted GeoTIFFs, not of members inside the archive, so they verify the local copies but not the archive itself.

s5p_l2_ch4_2018.product: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI Level 2 methane, RPRO stream, L2__CH4___
s5p_l2_ch4_2018.version: processor 020400, homogeneous across every 2018 granule used; the mirror also carries these orbits at other versions and only the highest per orbit was kept
s5p_l2_ch4_2018.citation: Copernicus Sentinel-5P (processed by ESA), TROPOMI Level 2 Methane total column products. Version 02. European Space Agency. doi:10.5270/S5P-3lcdqiv
s5p_l2_ch4_2018.licence: Copernicus open and free data policy; the MEEO mirror redistributes the ESA products unchanged and states no separate licence
s5p_l2_ch4_2018.notes: NO CONTENT CHECKSUM IS AVAILABLE FOR THIS SOURCE and the archive sha256 is null for that reason rather than because one was not computed. Every S3 ETag the mirror returns is a multipart tag with a minus-N suffix, which is an MD5 of the concatenated part MD5s rather than of the object, and the part size the uploader used is not published, so the tag cannot be reproduced or checked. Verification is structural instead: each granule must open as netCDF4 and hold a PRODUCT group with the methane, qa_value, latitude and longitude variables. That is weaker than the MD5 verification the figshare and Science Data Bank entries carry, and re-fetching cannot be proven to return the same bytes. The two files listed here are the derived composite and its per-cell table, which ARE checksummed, so the outputs verify even though the inputs cannot. The 578 granules themselves are not retained: they total 28.9 GB and were streamed one at a time, gridded and deleted. Pixel values encode qa in stored uint8 units with scale_factor 0.01, and fill values must be read per variable from their own _FillValue attribute.
s5p_l2_ch4_2018.doi_note: Two ESA DOIs exist for this product and both resolve. 10.5270/S5P-3lcdqiv, registered 2021, resolves to the KNMI/SRON product page at tropomi.eu and is the value the granules themselves declare in identifier_product_doi. 10.5270/S5P-3p6lnwd, registered 2019, resolves to the ESA Copernicus catalogue page and was cited here previously. The granule metadata is authoritative for which product was actually read, so the tropomi.eu DOI is the one carried.

natural_earth_china_outline.product: Natural Earth 50 m admin-1 states and provinces with lakes, China only, dissolved to a single outline
natural_earth_china_outline.version: as bundled in the cartopy shapefile cache on this machine
natural_earth_china_outline.notes: Public domain. Extracted from ne_50m_admin_1_states_provinces_lakes in the local cartopy cache by scripts/extract_reference_geometry.py, filtered to the 31 features with admin = 'China' and dissolved into one geometry, written as EPSG:4326 GeoJSON. copernicus_dem_glo90_yrd.product: Copernicus DEM GLO-90, 80 one-degree tiles over the study box, shaded and committed as relief
copernicus_dem_glo90_yrd.citation: European Space Agency, Sinergise (2021). Copernicus Global Digital Elevation Model. Distributed by OpenTopography and by the AWS Open Data registry.
copernicus_dem_glo90_yrd.version: GLO-90 as served by the copernicus-dem-90m S3 bucket, retrieved 2026-09-08; the bucket does not version its tiles
copernicus_dem_glo90_yrd.licence: Free of charge for any use, worldwide and without limit in time, including reproduction, distribution, communication to the public, adaptation and modification. Attribution is REQUIRED.
copernicus_dem_glo90_yrd.required_notice: produced using Copernicus WorldDEM™-90 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved
copernicus_dem_glo90_yrd.required_liability_notice: The organisations in charge of the Copernicus programme by law or by delegation do not incur any liability for any use of the Copernicus WorldDEM™-90
copernicus_dem_glo90_yrd.notes: Fetched by scripts/fetch_copernicus_dem.py into the gitignored data/raw/copernicus_dem/ (80 tiles, 408 MB) and turned into the committed hillshade by scripts/build_map_reference.py. What is committed is the shaded relief, not the elevation model. The bucket for GLO-90 is copernicus-dem-90m; copernicus-dem-30m serves GLO-30 and an identical readme, so the readme can be read from the wrong bucket without noticing. In a tile name, 10 is GLO-30's arc-second spacing and 30 is GLO-90's, which is the opposite of the two bucket names. Two cautions from the readme, both checked here rather than assumed. Ocean areas have no tiles and height may be assumed zero there: measured, 20 of the 100 tiles over the padded box are absent and all 20 are offshore, and they are filled with zero. Pixel spacing varies with LATITUDE, not longitude, and only above 50 degrees; at 26.9 to 35.3 N every one of the 80 tiles is 1200 by 1200 at 1/1200 degree in both axes, so the 1:5 height-to-width ratio that motivates cubic resampling in some derived products is not reachable from this study area. Cubic was used anyway, being right for a 3.9x decimation, and the tile seams were checked anyway: over the rugged 27 to 29.5 N band the mean second difference along tile-edge columns is 0.989 of its value elsewhere under cubic and 1.041 under bilinear, so neither shows a seam artefact. The DEM is warped onto a grid whose pixels are square in ground metres at 31.075 N, so gdaldem's single -s scale is exact in both axes; without that, east-west slope is under-weighted by 1/cos(31.075) = 17 percent. Shading is gdaldem hillshade -s 111120 -multidirectional -z 1.6 -compute_edges at GDAL 3.11.4. The required notice above is quoted verbatim from Article 6(b) of the Copernicus WorldDEM-90 licence, which applies because a hillshade is adapted data; the liability notice is Article 6(c), which applies because this repository redistributes a derived product.

natural_earth_hypsometric_inset.product: Natural Earth 50 m cross-blended hypsometric tints with shaded relief, clipped to the locator inset and warped to the project equal-area conic
natural_earth_hypsometric_inset.version: Natural Earth raster 2.0.0, as stated in HYP_50M_SR_W.VERSION.txt in the downloaded archive
natural_earth_hypsometric_inset.licence: Public domain, no attribution required, no restriction on redistribution or derivative works.
natural_earth_hypsometric_inset.notes: The global raster is 10800 by 5400, which is 30 pixels per degree. The inset is about 4.6 cm wide across 64 degrees, or 543 pixels at 300 dpi, so the committed clip is reduced to 16 px/deg and warped onto CHINA_ALBERS. The 10 m raster was measured rather than assumed: it is 21600 by 10800, 60 px/deg exactly, which is 465 pixels across the 7.75 degree study box against the main panel's 1205, so it is used for the inset and not for the main panel. Hypsometric here and grey relief in the main panel, because nothing is drawn over the inset.

natural_earth_places_yrd.product: Natural Earth 10 m populated places, filtered to the four study provinces' admin-1 capitals
natural_earth_places_yrd.version: Natural Earth vector 5.1.2, as stated in ne_10m_populated_places.VERSION.txt in the downloaded archive
natural_earth_places_yrd.notes: The selection rule is SCALERANK <= 4 and FEATURECLA == 'Admin-1 capital' and ADM1NAME in the four study provinces, which yields Shanghai, Nanjing, Hangzhou and Hefei. A bare scale-rank threshold cannot produce this set: Shanghai is rank 0, Nanjing and Hangzhou are rank 2 and Hefei is rank 4, so a threshold reaching Hefei also reaches fourteen other places in the box, among them Zaozhuang and Linyi in Shandong and Nanchang in Jiangxi. Suzhou, Wuxi and Ningbo are rank 4 and are deliberately left off: Suzhou and Wuxi are 0.35 degrees apart, which is 4.6 mm on the drawn panel, and both sit in the same cluster as Shanghai. 57 places fall in the study box in total. Unlike the province and land layers, this one was NOT in the local cartopy cache, which holds only physical and admin boundary layers, so it was fetched.

natural_earth_context_layers.product: Natural Earth admin-1 units neighbouring the study region, and admin-0 land boundary lines across the locator inset
natural_earth_context_layers.version: as bundled in the cartopy shapefile cache on this machine
natural_earth_context_layers.notes: yrd_neighbours.geojson is every admin-1 unit with admin = 'China' whose geometry intersects the drawn extent and which is not a study province, clipped to the padded box: Fujian, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi and Shandong. Selected by intersection, not hand-listed. From the 10 m layer. inset_boundaries.geojson is every feature of ne_50m_admin_0_boundary_lines_land intersecting the inset extent, 59 lines, UNFILTERED. The previous inset drew the 31 admin-1 units filed under admin = 'China' in the 50 m layer, which excluded Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau by inheritance rather than by choice -- and not even by the mechanism the reference README described, since the 50 m admin-1 layer has no Taiwan, Hong Kong or Macau features to exclude; only the 10 m layer carries them, as 21, 1 and 1 units against China's 32. Nothing is filtered now and no country is named or filled. This layer carries no Hong Kong or Macau feature at all, and Taiwan appears only as a coastline in the hypsometric raster. Natural Earth classes 6 of the 59 lines as 'Disputed (please verify)' and ships 33 per-country viewpoint fields including FCLASS_CN and FCLASS_TW, which is the source's own statement that the classification depends on who is asked.

blended_tropomi_gosat_2018.product: Blended TROPOMI+GOSAT methane, L2__CH4___, BLND stream
blended_tropomi_gosat_2018.version: processor 020400, matching every 2018 granule the operational composite used; the product manual scopes its correction to 02.04.00, 02.05.00 and 02.06.00
blended_tropomi_gosat_2018.citation: Balasus, N., Jacob, D. J., Lorente, A., Maasakkers, J. D., Parker, R. J., Boesch, H., Chen, Z., Kelp, M. M., Nesser, H., and Varon, D. J. (2023), A blended TROPOMI+GOSAT satellite data product for atmospheric methane using machine learning to correct retrieval biases, Atmospheric Measurement Techniques 16, 3787-3807, doi:10.5194/amt-16-3787-2023
blended_tropomi_gosat_2018.licence: From the AWS Registry of Open Data entry, verbatim: "There are no restrictions on the use of this data, but please contact nicholasbalasus@g.harvard.edu before its use in a publication." The product user manual asks more broadly: "please contact me if you plan to use the data in your research so that proper acknowledgements can be made." THE AUTHOR HAS NOT BEEN CONTACTED. That is a step for whoever publishes from this, and it is recorded here rather than assumed done.
blended_tropomi_gosat_2018.doi_note: Registry of Open Data listing at registry.opendata.aws/blended-tropomi-gosat-methane; product user manual at github.com/nicholasbalasus/write_blended_files/blob/main/PUM.md, dated 10 January 2026. A Harvard Dataverse copy exists at dataverse.harvard.edu/dataverse/blended-tropomi-gosat-methane and serves anonymously, but the bucket's own README records that maintenance of it stopped on 7 February 2024, so AWS is the live route.
blended_tropomi_gosat_2018.notes: NO CONTENT CHECKSUM IS AVAILABLE FOR 34 PERCENT OF THIS SOURCE and the archive sha256 is null for that reason. Of the 3,436 keys for 2018, 2,254 carry a single-part MD5 ETag that reproduces (verified on one object) and 1,182 carry a multipart tag that cannot; the threshold is exactly 8 MiB. No x-amz-checksum header is returned even with checksum mode enabled. Verification is structural for the remainder: the file must open as HDF5, carry the product's own Title attribute, and hold methane_mixing_ratio_blended, latitude, longitude and qa_value at the root. The files are FLAT ROOTED, with no netCDF groups, and hold only the soundings with qa_value == 1.0; src.methane.blended reads them and src.methane.grid.read_soundings cannot. They carry the operational values unaltered alongside the new variable: for orbit 03019 the maximum absolute difference against the retained operational granule was exactly zero on latitude, longitude, both operational methane variables and surface_albedo_SWIR across all 64,891 soundings. Three of the seven covariates this project grids are absent from these files -- eastward_wind, northward_wind and solar_zenith_angle -- which costs nothing for the analysis, because those covariates are already committed in methane_covariates_2018.csv over the identical soundings. Only the 223 orbits that carried an in-box sounding were read, and only four variables from each, over HTTP range requests: 335.6 MB in 1,385 requests against 23.08 GiB for the year. The granules are not retained.

tccon_hefei_ggg2020_r1.product: TCCON data from Hefei (PRC), Release GGG2020.R1; ground-based FTS column-averaged dry-air mole fractions
tccon_hefei_ggg2020_r1.version: GGG2020.R1, published 2023; record 2015-11-02 to 2025-12-30. A NEWER RELEASE EXISTS: GGG2020.1.R1, doi:10.14291/tccon.ggg2020p1.hefei01.R1, published 2026. This project's recorded counts were computed from R1 and are reproduced from R1; a submission should decide which release to cite.
tccon_hefei_ggg2020_r1.citation: Liu, C., Wang, W., and Sun, Y. (2022), TCCON data from Hefei, China, Release GGG2020R1, TCCON data archive, hosted by CaltechDATA, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA, U.S.A., doi:10.14291/tccon.ggg2020.hefei01.R1. The licence file gives this as "C., Liu, W. Wang, and Y Sun. 2022", which transposes the initials; the names are corrected here and the DOI is unchanged.
tccon_hefei_ggg2020_r1.licence: TCCON Data License, not an open licence, quoted from the deposit's own LICENSE.txt. Clause 4 verbatim: "All other rights, including redistribution, display, and publishing adaptations are reserved." THE STATION FILE IS THEREFORE NOT COMMITTED; data/processed/tccon_hefei_2018.csv carries derived counts and a network-tier recipe fetches the file. Clause 5 verbatim: "At a minimum of 4-6 weeks prior to the submission of a manuscript and 1-2 weeks prior to a public presentation of works that include TCCON data, you must contact the individuals listed on the DOI landing page via email and provide a description of the intended publication or presentation." tccon_hefei_ggg2020_r1.notes: Fetched to support three counts that reached four documents with no artefact behind them. The counts reproduce exactly: 2,767 retrievals on 44 days in 2018, and 9 days carrying both a retrieval and a TROPOMI overpass of the station's cell. NO GRANULES WERE DOWNLOADED: the days a granule covered the station cell come from the committed checkpoint's packed per-granule cell sets, so the 480 MB this recovery was priced at was not needed. The files listed here are NOT in version control and must not be committed; their digests are recorded so a re-fetch can be checked.
